title: Ex 8.10 · Complement of an intersection
prompt: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets inside a universal set $U$, and write $\overline{X} = U - X$ for the complement of a set $X$. Prove De Morgan's law $\overline{A \cap B} = \overline{A} \cup \overline{B}$. (Type the complement of $A$ as A'.)
answer_format: A chain of lines, each a set (like A ∪ (B ∩ C)) or a statement about an element x (like x ∈ A or x ∈ B). Each line must have exactly the same elements as the line before; start from the left side and end at the right side. Type the complement of A as A' (the universal set is U).
hints: x ∈ (A ∩ B)' says x is not in A ∩ B, that is, not (x ∈ A and x ∈ B).
Use De Morgan's law for logic: ∼(P ∧ Q) is the same as ∼P ∨ ∼Q. Note that the 'and' turns into an 'or'.
x ∉ A is the same as x ∈ A' (every element is in U). So x ∉ A or x ∉ B becomes x ∈ A' ∪ B'.
solution: Let $x \in U$. Then $x \in \overline{A \cap B}$ means $x \notin A \cap B$, that is, $\sim(x \in A \land x \in B)$.
By De Morgan's law, $\sim(P \land Q) = \,\sim P \lor \sim Q$, this is $x \notin A \lor x \notin B$.
Since $x \in U$, $x \notin A$ means $x \in \overline{A}$ and $x \notin B$ means $x \in \overline{B}$. So the statement is $x \in \overline{A} \cup \overline{B}$.
Every step was an equivalence, so $\overline{A \cap B} = \overline{A} \cup \overline{B}$. $\blacksquare$

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses Section 8.3 (proving A = B), the complement (Section 1.6) and De Morgan's laws for logic (Section 2.6).
